text: Mai, Lin, and Bo each bring a different item: a cup, fruit, or bread. Mai brings neither food item, and Lin does not bring bread. What does Bo bring?
explanation: Mai brings the cup. Lin must bring fruit, leaving bread for Bo.

text: At 9:00, a file starts downloading for five minutes while a printer starts an eight-minute job. Both run without interruption. When are both jobs finished?
explanation: The jobs run at the same time. The download ends at 9:05; the slower printer ends at 9:08.

text: Every draft with a red tag needs review. A draft needs review, but its tag is hidden. Must its tag be red?
choices: The rule does not tell us
explanation: The rule tells us what red tags require. It does not say that only red-tagged drafts need review.

text: You cut one straight ribbon into four separate pieces, making one cut at a time and never stacking or folding it. How many cuts are needed?
explanation: One piece becomes two after one cut. Each additional cut adds one piece, so three cuts make four.

text: Two closed jars contain only tea or only coffee, one of each. Their labels say tea and coffee, but both labels are wrong. What is in the jar labeled coffee?
explanation: Both labels are wrong and each jar holds just one drink. The coffee-labeled jar must hold tea.

text: A small bag holds at most six kilograms. The camera weighs two, the books three, and the speaker four. Which pair fits and uses the full weight allowance?
explanation: The camera and speaker weigh exactly six kilograms. The books with the speaker weigh seven; the camera with books uses only five.

text: Three friends can meet only on these days: An on Friday or Saturday, Bao on Saturday or Sunday, Chi on Friday or Saturday. Which day works for all three?
explanation: Saturday appears in all three lists. Bao is unavailable Friday, and An and Chi are unavailable Sunday.

text: A key is in exactly one of three boxes: blue, green, or gold. Exactly one statement is true: “It is in blue” and “It is not in gold.” Where is the key?
explanation: Blue makes both statements true; gold makes both false. Green makes only “not in gold” true.

text: Four friends each send one private greeting to every other friend. A greeting from An to Bao is separate from Bao to An. How many greetings are sent?
explanation: Each of four people sends three greetings. Four times three is twelve; each direction counts separately.

text: A zine has three steps: print, fold, and staple. Folding must follow printing, and stapling must follow folding. Which step is immediately before stapling?
explanation: The required order is print, fold, staple. Folding is the step directly before stapling.

text: A rhythm repeats clap, tap, tap, rest, starting at beat one. What happens on beat seven?
explanation: Beats five through eight repeat clap, tap, tap, rest. Beat seven is the second tap in that group.

text: A photo is twelve units wide and eight tall. You crop only its width to make a square, keeping the full height. How many width units must you remove in total?
explanation: The square must be eight units wide to match its height. Twelve minus eight leaves four units to remove in total.

text: The café is reached by either of two routes: a direct twelve-minute bus ride, or a four-minute metro ride plus a five-minute transfer and a two-minute walk. Which is quicker?
explanation: The metro route takes four plus five plus two, or eleven minutes. That is one minute less than twelve.

text: A train leaves at 8:50 and arrives at 9:15 the same morning. How long is the trip?
explanation: Ten minutes takes us to 9:00; fifteen more takes us to 9:15. The trip lasts twenty-five minutes.

text: A shuttle travels A, B, C, D, E in that order. You board at B and get off at E. Counting arrival at E but not boarding at B, how many stops do you reach?
explanation: After boarding at B, you reach C, D, and E: three stops.

text: A sequence alternates two steps: add three, then multiply by two. Starting at two gives 2, 5, 10, 13, 26. What comes next?
explanation: The step after multiplying is adding three. Twenty-six plus three is twenty-nine.

text: A jar has exactly three blue beads and two white beads. Without looking and without putting any back, how many must you take to guarantee two of the same color?
explanation: Two draws could give one of each color. The third bead must match one of the two colors already drawn.

text: In this card set, every triangle is striped. A card has no stripes. Which shape is ruled out by that rule?
explanation: A triangle must have stripes. Without stripes, this card cannot be a triangle; the rule says nothing about circles or squares.
